additional_info.subject: ID0441808-DC/SI-D/FR-[MP / P8 170001004] Charging Issue CRM:02678000159
additional_info.body:
Hello Théo, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
As you refered in the form, 4 chargers had this problem at the same time. This clearly indicates a problem upstream on the medium voltage cabinet or similar.
What I can see from the logs is that at your 18:00 the power is lost completely and we stop getting logs:
If the power loss was on the charger side, we wouldn't have lost all the logs and connection as it's from the 24V supply, in case of a failure in AC income, the Mainbreaker would trigger and we would see it.
From our side, it's clear that this issue was not caused by us. Please check if there was any sort of power outage in the area or similar.
Let me know if I answered to your questions and can close the ticket.
Thank you!!!
best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0441808-DC/SI-D/FR-[MP / P8 170001004] Charging Issue CRM:02678000159
additional_info.body:
Hello,
Thanks for your answer,
I also think that the problem came from the AC input and maybe from the grid our from our transformer.
I wanted to know if you had some clue of what happened in the logs, there was no complete power outage because clients on site told us that right after the black screen, the chargers started to boot up.
Is there is anything else that could help us understand what happened in the logs on one of the chargers ?
Thanks again for your help !
Kind regards,
Théo  SALMON
Chargé d’exploitation IRVE

additional_info.subject: ID0441808-DC/SI-D/FR-[MP / P8 170001004] Charging Issue CRM:02678000159
additional_info.body:
Hello Théo, good morning.
The only information I can provide is that when the PLC crashes completely, it must mean that there was something unrelated to the charger happening.
When these cases occur, we do not have any logging because the power supply is cut and therefore, the PLC cannot "dump" the logs since it's offline.
Unfortunately, I do not have the answer you wish. I can only mention that if it happened with 4 chargers simultaneosly, then the problem must be upstream.
Let me know if I answered to your questions and can close the ticket.
Thanks and have a nice day!
Best regards,
Francisco
